rv.q: Mulvaney delivers an entertaining, bold and colorful portrait — a play with music — of all her complexities, and the tumultuous life of someone who would rather perform and have fun than speak from podiums.
The Least Problematic Woman in the World is a 90-minute joy bomb.
Under the weight of the show's ambition, Dylan Mulvaney is a star.
Despite some flaws, Mulvaney shines as genuine, talented, and lovable. The Least Problematic Woman in the World is a campy, frothy good time with real heart.
Much of it lands. It helps that she’s willing to make fun of herself, such as the final song of self-acceptance.
The Least Problematic Woman… prioritizes comedy over clarity, so if you don't know Mulvaney, be sure to do some pre-show scrolling.
The performance was nothing short of spectacular, especially for a first preview.
It's a whole lot of fun — fearless, funny, and deeply human.
It was flashy, glitzy, glamorous, and irreverent— and it was also touching, raw, emotional, real, and utterly transformative.
Mulvaney's messy, marvelous, madcap life—and the show it inspired—are all the better for it.
It's a tour de force performance, full of personality, spunk, and playfulness that dramatize the nuances of her TikTok-documented pandemic-era transition.
Broadly engaging, this autobiographical show succeeds where others of this ilk often fail.
